newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury current sales match inflation.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury current sales match inflation.

text.p: British supermarket retailer J. Sainsbury Plc said on Wednesday that current like-for-like sales growth in its supermarkets, before petrol sales, was now "in lne with sales inflation of three percent."
Sainsburys saw half-year pretax profits slip to 393 million pounds ($631.5 million), within forecasts, from 456 million pounds previously and paid out a dividend of 3.5 pence, up from 3.4 pence.

The company, which announced its first fall in annual profits for 22 years earlier this year, said in a statement with the latest first-half results that gross margins are stable in supermarkets while in petrol they are improving.
Sainsbury said its Reward loyalty card, launched four months ago, was contributing between two and three percent of incremental sales, excluding the impact of Savercards last year.

The supermarket chain, pipped off the market leader slot by Tesco last year, said reduced gross margins and increased staffing during the second half of last year cut first half operating margins by 0.8 percent of sales.

Sainsbury, which last week announced plans to launch financial services with Bank of Scotland, said there would be a further "major development" with its Reward card soon and that it looked forward to "a strong Christmas trading season."
